title: Three Years After a Car Crash Nearly Killed Him, Rishabh Pant Has Played His 50th Test for India.
excerpt: Only MS Dhoni and Syed Kirmani have kept wicket in more Tests for India. Pant is 28. He hit three sixes in one over on Saturday.
body:
On December 30, 2022, Rishabh Pant's car hit the central divider on the Delhi-Dehradun highway, flipped over, and caught fire. He broke his knee. He tore a ligament. He had cuts on his forehead and his back. The doctors said he was lucky to be alive.

On Saturday in Mullanpur, he walked out to bat in his 50th Test match for India, hit three sixes off Abdul Malik in a single over, and finished the day unbeaten on 50 off 70 balls.

## The Club of Three

https://x.com/RishabhPant17/status/2062868051230593505

With this appearance, Pant became only the third Indian wicketkeeper in history to play 50 or more Test matches. The other two names on the list explain why this matters:

| Wicketkeeper | Tests | Years Active |
|---|---|---|
| MS Dhoni | 90 | 2005–2014 |
| Syed Kirmani | 88 | 1976–1986 |
| **Rishabh Pant** | **50*** | **2018–Present** |

Kiran More, India's keeper through the late 1980s and early 1990s, played 49. Farokh Engineer, the dashing keeper from the 1960s and 1970s, managed 46. Pant has passed them all at the age of 28, with potentially a decade of Test cricket ahead of him.

## The Recovery That Defined a Generation

The car crash happened between India's Test series in Bangladesh and their tour of Australia. Pant was in the form of his life — he had scored a century at Edgbaston, match-winning knocks in Australia, and the famous 89 not out at the Gabba that won India the 2021 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

What followed was 14 months of rehabilitation. The knee reconstruction was complex. The ligament repair was delicate. There were weeks where he could not walk, months where he could not run, and a sustained period where the question was not when he would play cricket again but whether he would play at all.

He returned in the 2024 IPL. He was not the same player — he was more considered, less reckless, still explosive but now with a filter. He played through the 2024 T20 World Cup, was part of India's title-winning squad, and then quietly continued rebuilding his red-ball game.

## Saturday's Innings

At Mullanpur, Pant came in at 247/3 with India already in a dominant position. What he did with that position was instructive. He played defensively for the first 40 balls — unusually restrained for a man whose natural instinct is to hit everything over mid-wicket.

Then, in the 68th over, he faced Abdul Malik and decided the waiting was done. Three sixes — massive, premeditated, launched with the full weight of his body behind each swing. The crowd roared. It was the Pant they remembered, the one from before the crash, the one who plays cricket as if it is a personal argument with gravity.

But then he did something the old Pant rarely did. He went back to defence. He blocked the next few deliveries with soft hands, played out the over after that with a dead bat, and let Gill continue scoring at the other end. They added 121 runs together in an unbroken fourth-wicket stand. Pant's 50 came just before stumps.

## What the Diaspora Sees

For NRI cricket fans who stayed up through the night to watch Pant at the Gabba, his 50th Test is a checkpoint in a story they have been following for years. The car crash made global headlines — it was covered by CNN, BBC, ESPN. Indian diaspora communities in the US organised prayer meetings. When he came back, the ovation at the 2024 IPL was felt in living rooms from Edison to Fremont to Hounslow.

Now, at 28, he is entering what should be the prime years of his career. If he stays fit, Dhoni's record of 90 Tests as a keeper is within reach. More importantly, India's Test team — transitioning beyond Kohli and Rohit — needs Pant to be the senior figure who anchors the batting order and brings the swagger that makes Test cricket worth watching at 3 AM in California.

## What's Next

India are 368/3 at stumps. Pant and Gill will resume on Day 2 against an Afghan attack that looked exhausted by the end of Day 1. A century is on the cards. But even if it does not come, the milestone is already recorded: 50 Tests, three years after a crash that nearly ended everything.

The wicketkeeper who almost did not make it back is still here. He is still hitting sixes. He is still keeping for India. And he is only 28.
